tasks.text: One slice rebuilds the registry mirror from the chain. Checked means demonstrated by an executable check on the candidate, not merely written; unchecked items are open work rather than pending paperwork.

landed-in-the-audited-candidate.text: The audited candidate carries the mirror checkpoint, the follower over the pinned chain follower, per-fold and tip root equality with an executed failure control, atomic mirror writing, checkpoint resume, the follow and rebuild surfaces, the devnet end-to-end check in continuous integration, and the rewritten onboarding paragraph.
The restored specification and reconciled plan are recorded here as ticket-owner work. They describe the candidate; they do not validate it.

open-repair-batch.text: Seven repair items remain open, each carrying its failing and passing criterion in the adjudicated batch: bind every replay arm, make the offchain failure classes reachable by continuous integration, control the named refusal classes, exercise the rollback reset and genuine legacy mirror loading, invoke the shipped command entry points, decide the mirror file mode, and leave the manifest schema untouched.

open-acceptance-dependencies.text: Two dependencies stay open regardless of how the repairs land. The preprod observation is blocked pending a verified milestone handoff and writer assignment, so it is unobserved rather than satisfied. The bootstrap starting point needs a manifest chain point owned outside this ticket, and recording the deviation closes only the documentation task, never the requirement.

slice.text: The slice is owner mode. A separate accountable implementer owns the change, and independent audit of the candidate and the changed gates is required before trunk; the implementer does not accept its own work.
